Deniz held Grandma's hand and walked along the garden path. The path went past tall grass to the little observation shelter. Deniz liked this walk. But today something looked different. The shallow pool by the shelter was lower. The water did not reach the painted stone marker. Usually the water touched the blue line on the stone. Deniz frowned a little. "Why is the water lower?" Deniz asked. "Let's look carefully," said Grandma. "Looking helps before guessing." Deniz nodded.

From the shelter, Deniz looked and looked. Near the small inlet grate on the public side, leaves and twigs had gathered in a little pile. The soil by the path was dry and cracked, like a dry cookie. Deniz remembered the week: sunny day after sunny day, very warm, no rain at all. Some plants near the water had yellow and brown leaves now. Deniz pointed at each thing. "I see leaves. I see dry dirt. I see yellow leaves." Grandma listened and smiled. She did not say the answer.

Deniz thought hard. Once, on another sunny day, a puddle got smaller and smaller until it was gone. "Maybe the warm days made the water smaller here too," Deniz said. "Maybe." Then Deniz looked at the yellow leaves. "Maybe the plants are just changing for the season. Plants do that." Deniz looked at the pile by the grate. "Maybe the leaves and sticks stop some water there. I don't know." Grandma nodded. "Good looking," she said. "Shall we look once more, close to the path?" "Yes," said Deniz.

Deniz and Grandma walked a little way on the marked path. From the path, Deniz could see the inlet grate. The leaves and twigs sat right beside it, all close together. The water was low near the painted stone marker, and low farther along the visible edge too. The tall reeds stood quiet and still, and Deniz did not go near them. "The pile is by the grate," Deniz said. "But the water is low in lots of places." Grandma stayed close the whole time.

Deniz had an idea. "Grandma, let's tell the garden caretaker," Deniz said. "I can say what I saw." Grandma found Ms. Rosa, the caretaker, by the tool shed. Deniz told her, in small words: "The pool is lower than the stone. The days were warm and dry. The plants are turning yellow for the season. And leaves and twigs are piled by the inlet grate." Ms. Rosa knelt down. "Thank you for looking so carefully," she said. "I will check the inlet safely." Deniz watched from the path while Ms. Rosa walked over. Deniz felt warm inside. Someone had listened.

Deniz and Grandma walked back on the same path. A bird sang. The reeds moved in the soft wind. The wetland went on being a wetland. "We can look again next time," Deniz said. "The water might change for more than one reason." "Yes," said Grandma. "And careful looking helps us take care of it." Deniz smiled. Looking twice was a good way to help.

Deniz başını salladı.

Deniz her şeyi tek tek gösterdi.

Büyükanne dinledi ve gülümsedi. Cevabı söylemedi.

“İyi baktın,” dedi. “Yolun yakınına bir kez daha bakalım mı?”

“Evet,” dedi Deniz.

Deniz’in aklına bir fikir geldi.

“Büyükanne, bahçeye bakan kişiye söyleyelim,” dedi Deniz. “Gördüklerimi anlatabilirim.”

Büyükanne, alet kulübesinin yanında bahçeye bakan Bayan Rosa’yı buldu. Deniz ona küçük cümlelerle anlattı:

“Havuzdaki su taştan daha aşağıda. Günler sıcak ve kuruydu. Mevsim değiştiği için bitkiler sararıyor. Bir de su giriş ızgarasının yanında yapraklar ve çalı çırpı birikmiş.”

Bayan Rosa diz çöktü.

“Dikkatlice baktığın için teşekkür ederim,” dedi. “Su girişini güvenli bir şekilde kontrol edeceğim.”

Deniz, Bayan Rosa oraya yürürken onu yoldan izledi. Deniz’in içi sıcacık oldu. Biri onu dinlemişti.

“Evet,” dedi Büyükanne. “Dikkatlice bakmak, ona iyi bakmamıza yardım eder.”

Deniz gülümsedi. İki kez bakmak, yardım etmenin güzel bir yoluydu.

Deniz walked with Mama along the marked path through the community garden. Bees buzzed near purple flowers. At the little observation shelter, Deniz looked down at the shallow pool. The water usually reached a blue mark painted on a stone. Today, the blue mark was dry. “Why is it lower?” Deniz asked. Mama did not guess. “What can we notice?” she asked. Deniz stayed inside the shelter and leaned forward to look closely.

The pool looked smaller than it had on their last visit. Mama and Deniz remembered the dry, warm days that week. Deniz also remembered a puddle that had shrunk after a sunny afternoon. “Maybe the warm days changed the water,” Deniz said. Beside the pool, some plants were yellow and brown. Deniz followed the marked path toward the reed edge. Near the public-side inlet grate, loose leaves and small twigs had gathered in a clump. The water there moved only a little. Beyond it, tall reeds grew close together. The path ended before them, so Deniz stopped. Deniz could not see what was inside and did not go closer. “The warm days could matter,” Deniz said. “And these sticks could matter. Maybe there is more than one reason.”

Deniz hurried back to Mama, but stayed on the path. “What did you see?” Mama asked. Deniz counted on four fingers. “Lower water. Dry, warm days. Yellow and brown plants. Leaves and twigs by the grate.” “What do we know?” Mama asked. Deniz thought. “The leaves are near the slow water. But we do not know everything.” Then Deniz said, “Maybe the leaves changed some water, and maybe the warm days changed some too.” Deniz chose to tell the garden helper and leave the reeds alone.

Mama found Ms. Lee, the community garden helper. Deniz showed her the inlet from the public path. Ms. Lee checked it carefully. With Mama beside her, she removed only the loose leaves and small twigs caught against the public-side grate. Deniz watched and kept both hands away from the water. Soon, a small trickle slipped through more freely. “It moves better now!” Deniz said. The leaves had affected the inlet. Still, the pool did not rise to the blue mark. The warm weather and seasonal changes might matter too.

On a later visit, Deniz checked again from the shelter and the marked path. The inlet was open, and the little trickle still moved. The pool was still lower than before. “Maybe the warm days, the season, and the blocked grate all mattered,” Deniz said. A bird called. Insects skimmed the water. Deniz looked at the blue mark once more. “We can look again another day.”

scenes.prose: Deniz walked with Mama along the marked path through the community garden. Bees buzzed near purple flowers. At the little observation shelter, Deniz looked down at the shallow pool. The water usually reached a blue mark painted on a stone. Today, the blue mark was dry. “Why is it lower?” Deniz asked. Mama did not guess. “What can we notice?” she asked. Deniz stayed inside the shelter and leaned forward to look closely.

The pool looked smaller than it had on their last visit. Mama and Deniz remembered the dry, warm days that week. Deniz also remembered a puddle that had shrunk after a sunny afternoon. “Maybe the warm days changed the water,” Deniz said. Beside the pool, some plants were yellow and brown. Others were still green. “Maybe the plants are changing with the season,” said Deniz. But warm days and changing leaves did not explain everything yet.

Deniz followed the marked path toward the reed edge. Near the public-side inlet grate, loose leaves and small twigs had gathered in a clump. The water there moved only a little. Beyond it, tall reeds grew close together. The path ended before them, so Deniz stopped. Deniz could not see what was inside and did not go closer. “The warm days could matter,” Deniz said. “And these sticks could matter. Maybe there is more than one reason.”

Deniz hurried back to Mama, but stayed on the path. “What did you see?” Mama asked. Deniz counted on four fingers. “Lower water. Dry, warm days. Yellow and brown plants. Leaves and twigs by the grate.” “What do we know?” Mama asked. Deniz thought. “The leaves are near the slow water. But we do not know everything.” Then Deniz said, “Maybe the leaves changed some water, and maybe the warm days changed some too.” Deniz chose to tell the garden helper and leave the reeds alone.

Mama found Ms. Lee, the community garden helper. Deniz showed her the inlet from the public path. Ms. Lee checked it carefully. With Mama beside her, she removed only the loose leaves and small twigs caught against the public-side grate. Deniz watched and kept both hands away from the water. Soon, a small trickle slipped through more freely. “It moves better now!” Deniz said. The leaves had affected the inlet. Still, the pool did not rise to the blue mark. The warm weather and seasonal changes might matter too.

On a later visit, Deniz checked again from the shelter and the marked path. The inlet was open, and the little trickle still moved. The pool was still lower than before. “Maybe the warm days, the season, and the blocked grate all mattered,” Deniz said. A bird called. Insects skimmed the water. Deniz looked at the blue mark once more. “We can look again another day.”

Mama nods. "The plants change when the season turns. Is that the same as the water going down?" Deniz thinks. "I don't know. Maybe more than one thing is happening."

Deniz stands on the path and points. "The sky was dry. The leaves and twigs sit by the grate. The plants turned yellow." Deniz counts on four small fingers. "Maybe the sun. Maybe the water can't get past the leaves. Maybe people did something. Maybe it's just the season." Mama listens. "Good wonderings. We can only act on what we can see." Deniz looks at the inlet by the path. "We can tell someone about the leaves there. The deep reeds are not a place for us to go."

The garden helper is nearby, watering the flowers. Deniz squeezes Mama's hand. Mama nods, and Deniz speaks up. "Leaves and twigs are by the inlet." The helper smiles and gets a small rake. scenes.prose: Deniz is four. Deniz loves the wetland garden. Today Deniz walks with Mama along the marked path they know well, past the flowers and the buzzing bees, all the way to the observation shelter. Deniz looks at the shallow pool. The painted stone marker stands by the water. Last time, the water reached right up to the marker. Today, the water stops far below it. Deniz asks, "Why is the water down?" Mama smiles. "Good question. Let's look closely and see."

Deniz walks a little way along the marked path and stops. "I see leaves," Deniz says. "I see twigs, too." A few leaves and twigs sit in a small pile by the inlet grate, where water flows into the pool. Deniz does not touch the grate. Deniz looks at the reeds. The water beside them is very shallow. Deniz stays right on the path. "I wonder why the leaves sit in a pile," Deniz says. Mama nods. "You saw leaves and twigs by the grate. You saw shallow water by the reeds. Let's remember these clues and find more."

Deniz thinks and thinks. "I remember hot days," Deniz says. "All week the sun was warm and the sky stayed dry." Then Deniz remembers something else. "One day, my little puddle got smaller and smaller after a sunny afternoon." Deniz looks at the garden plants. Some leaves are turning yellow and orange. "Plants can change too," Deniz says. Mama nods. "The plants change when the season turns. Is that the same as the water going down?" Deniz thinks. "I don't know. Maybe more than one thing is happening."

Deniz stands on the path and points. "The sky was dry. The leaves and twigs sit by the grate. The plants turned yellow." Deniz counts on four small fingers. "Maybe the sun. Maybe the water can't get past the leaves. Maybe people did something. Maybe it's just the season." Mama listens. "Good wonderings. We can only act on what we can see." Deniz looks at the inlet by the path. "We can tell someone about the leaves there. The deep reeds are not a place for us to go."

The garden helper is nearby, watering the flowers. Deniz squeezes Mama's hand. Mama nods, and Deniz speaks up. "Leaves and twigs are by the inlet." The helper smiles and gets a small rake. Deniz watches from the marked path. The helper softly lifts the leaves and twigs away from the grate. Only the pile. The plants and the reed edge stay just as they were. A little water slips through the open grate. "The water can move now," Deniz says. "But maybe the dry days and the season are part of it too."

Back at the shelter, Deniz looks once more. The water, the marker, the yellow plants, the reeds. "Maybe the dry days. Maybe the leaves. Maybe the season," Deniz says softly. "Maybe all of them together." Mama takes Deniz's hand. "We can come back and look again." "Yes," says Deniz. "The wetland can keep being a wetland." They walk home along the marked path together.
